title: Passive Reporting Verbs
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Esta estructura es fundamental en el periodismo, los reportes financieros y las reuniones ejecutivas para sonar objetivo y profesional.

parts.visual:
Usamos la pasiva con verbos de reporte (say, think, believe, expect, report) para dar información sin especificar quién la dijo. Suena formal y objetivo. 
Forma 1 (It is... that): 
- It IS SAID that the company is bankrupt. (Se dice que la empresa está en quiebra). 
- It WAS EXPECTED that profits would fall. (Se esperaba que las ganancias cayeran).
parts.audio: We use the passive voice with reporting verbs like say, think, believe, expect, and report, to give information without specifying who said it. It sounds formal and objective. Form 1: It is said that the company is bankrupt. It was expected that profits would fall.

parts.visual:
Forma 2 (Sujeto + pasiva + to): 
- The company IS SAID TO BE bankrupt. (Se dice que la empresa está en quiebra). 
- The CEO IS EXPECTED TO RESIGN tomorrow. (Se espera que el CEO renuncie mañana). 
- They ARE BELIEVED TO HAVE lost millions. (Se cree que ellos han perdido millones).
parts.audio: Form 2, Subject plus passive plus 'to' infinitive: The company is said to be bankrupt. The CEO is expected to resign tomorrow. They are believed to have lost millions.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la forma correcta de la pasiva impersonal.

questions.question: ____ is expected that the merger will be successful. (Se espera).
questions.explanation: It is expected that... (estructura impersonal con It).

questions.question: The CEO is expected ____ tomorrow. (Que renuncie).
questions.explanation: Sujeto + is expected + to infinitive (to resign).

questions.question: It ____ that the company will go public next year. (Se rumorea).
questions.explanation: It is rumored that... (pasiva de rumor).

questions.question: The economy is believed ____ recovering. (Estar recuperándose).
It ____ that the new law will affect taxes. (Se piensa/cree).
They are reported ____ millions in the last quarter. (Haber perdido).
questions.explanation: Acción pasada (haber perdido) = to have + participio.

questions.question: The meeting ____ to start at 9:00 AM. (Se supone).
questions.explanation: Is supposed to = se supone que.

questions.question: ____ is believed that the competitor will launch a new product. (Se cree).
The suspect is known ____ the country. (Haber dejado).
It was reported that the factory ____ closed. (Había sido).
questions.explanation: Reporte en pasado sobre una acción anterior: had been closed.

questions.question: The new software is said ____ very user-friendly. (Ser).
It ____ that the interest rates will go up. (Ha sido anunciado).
questions.explanation: It has been announced that... (Present perfect pasivo).

questions.question: The project is expected ____ by Friday. (Estar terminado).
____ is said that she works 14 hours a day. (Se dice).
She is said ____ 14 hours a day. (Trabajar).
The company was estimated ____ a value of $2 billion. (Tener).
It is generally ____ that early investments are risky. (Acordado/Aceptado).
He is supposed ____ the best lawyer in the city. (Ser).
The board members are believed ____ a secret meeting right now. (Estar teniendo).
questions.explanation: To be + -ing (para una acción en progreso ahora mismo).

questions.question: It ____ confirmed that the contract is signed. (Ha sido).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra faltante para la pasiva impersonal.

questions.question: ____ is said that he is rich. (Pronombre neutro)
He is said ____ be rich. (Preposición infinita)
The company is expected to ____ (be) sold. (Estar/Ser)
It is ____ (believe) that prices will rise. (Se cree con d al final)
They are reported to ____ (have) lost the money. (Haber)
It is ____ (suppose) to rain today. (Se supone)
The meeting is supposed ____ start at 9. (Preposición infinita)
It has ____ announced that the CEO resigned. (Sido)
She is known to ____ (be) a great manager. (Ser)
It is ____ (rumor) that they will merge. (Se rumorea)
